_note: App-authored Nether Boss threat analysis, keyed by the extract's boss key (bosses.json type nether_boss). Every claim is taken from the code behaviour in _su_extract data/model/bosses.json (boss_traits[].behaviour / code_vs_text) and code/NETHER_BOSS_BEHAVIOR_FINDINGS.md, plus game rules from TIMELINE_FINDINGS (timeline moves), EFFECT_FORMULAS (crit, Defending) and the rune research (sourceless damage ticks, Shelled vs indirect). A value may be a string or {"1":..,"2":..,"3":..} per tier; "tiers" limits a threat to those tiers. notes = code-vs-text clarify notes per tier ("all" = every tier), shown under the boss trait of the lead creature, or of the creature named in "_unit". build-data validates every key against bosses.json.

title.1: Permanent Bleeding that spreads
title.2: Bleeding from the highest stat, spread to everyone
title.3: Double Bleeding from the highest stat, spread to everyone

what.1: Your creatures always have Bleeding: any creature without it gets it back. When one takes its Bleeding damage at the start of its turn, each of its living allies takes the same amount.
what.2: Your creatures always have Bleeding, and its damage is based on the bleeding creature's highest stat instead of its Health. Every tick is copied to each of its living allies.
what.3: Your creatures always have Bleeding based on their highest stat, it ticks twice at the start of each turn, and every tick is copied to each of their living allies.

why.1: A creature's own tick is 30% of its current Health, but the copies are flat amounts from its allies' ticks, so every creature takes up to five extra hits a round and a low-Health one can die to its teammates' Bleeding. Removing Bleeding only lasts until the trait gives it back. Heal the whole party every round or kill Kiichi fast.
why.2: Based on the highest stat, Bleeding no longer shrinks as Health drops, and the creature with the biggest stat bleeds hardest and copies that to the whole party. Fewer creatures means fewer copies: each tick is spread to every living ally.
why.3: Two ticks per turn means two rounds of copies: each creature's turn start hits the whole party twice for a share of its highest stat. This is a race; kill Kiichi before the copies stack up.

what.3: Every creature on Ianne's side takes 5% less damage for each time it has been damaged this battle, up to 80% less.

why.3: Area spells and splash damage raise every enemy's count at once. Focus one creature at a time with big single hits so each one dies before its reduction climbs.

what.3: After any creature on its side takes damage, every creature on its side gains Shelled.

title.2: Locks on to two and one-shots

threats.why: Rapture hits your whole party for a massive amount and leaves them Weak (50% less damage dealt) and Vulnerable (50% more damage taken), every one of its turns. Cleanse often or kill it fast.

title.2: Starts with an army of minions

title.1: Attacking Scorns you, casting Silences you
title.2: Each action locks it out and drains the stat
title.3: Each action locks it out, and the locks stack

what.1: After one of your creatures attacks, it is Scorned for 2 turns (can't attack). After it casts a spell, it gets Silence for 2 turns (can't cast).
what.2: After one of your creatures attacks, it is Scorned for 2 turns and loses 35% of its current Attack. After it casts, it gets Silence for 2 turns and loses 35% of its current Intelligence.
what.3: As tier 2, and Scorned and Silence no longer replace each other, so a creature can have both.

why.1: Scorned and Silence normally overwrite each other, so alternate: attack, then cast while Scorned (the new Silence replaces the Scorn), then attack again. Creatures that can only do one thing sit out while locked.
why.2: Alternating still works (the new debuff replaces the old one), but every action costs 35% of the stat it used and it compounds: four attacks leave about 18% of your Attack. Hit hardest on the first actions.
why.3: A creature that attacks and then casts ends up unable to do either. Plan each creature's actions so it never needs both, and front-load damage: every action drains 35% of the stat it used.

why.3: 36 attacks a round: +900% by the end of the first round. Every creature's turn feeds it six attacks, so kill it with your first actions.

title.2: Hit one, the other five hit back

what.3: When a Sadomasochist takes damage from one of your creatures, every other living Sadomasochist attacks that creature 3 times.

2: The text limits the crit and can't-be-dodged effect to the counterattacks; in code it applies to every attack and hit from their side.
3: The text limits the crit and can't-be-dodged effect to the counterattacks; in code it applies to every attack and hit from their side.

why.1: Bring creatures of several classes so someone can always hit. Damage with no source creature skips the shield: Poison, Burned and Bleeding ticks always get through.
why.2: Bring creatures of several classes so someone can always hit. Its side is immune to debuffs now, so damage over time can't be applied.
why.3: Only attacks and spells from the matching class work: debuffs and indirect damage are both blocked. Bring all five classes, or creatures that can change class.

what.3: Every creature on Chroma's side is immune to debuffs and takes no indirect damage.

title.1: A full-Health Barrier every turn

why.3: Mending heals 30% at each turn start and Leeching heals 25% of the damage they deal, on top of the Barriers. Focus fire hard; spread damage achieves nothing.
